title: A Podcast on Traveling Alone for the First Time
script: Host: [warmly] Welcome back to the show. Today my guest is Maya, who just returned from three weeks of solo travel. Thanks for joining me, Maya.
Guest: Thank you for having me. I'm still a little jet-lagged, but happy to talk about it.
Host: [thoughtful] What made you decide to travel alone for the first time?
Guest: Honestly, I kept waiting for a friend to be free at the same time, and it never happened.
Host: [honestly] So you finally just booked the ticket yourself?
Guest: Exactly. I researched the route, chose reviewed accommodation, bought suitable insurance, and then booked the flight.
Host: [carefully] Were you nervous before you left?
Guest: Extremely nervous. I almost canceled the trip twice in the week before I flew.
Host: [curious] What helped you get on that plane anyway?
Guest: A friend told me, you can always come home early if you hate it. That made it feel less permanent.
Host: [relieved] What surprised you most once you actually arrived?
Guest: How much planning mattered. I kept document copies, used trusted transport, and checked in with family at agreed times.
Host: [reflective] Did you ever feel lonely during those three weeks?
Guest: Yes, a few evenings, especially eating dinner alone at first. That part took practice.
Host: [encouraging] How did you handle those lonely moments?
Guest: I started bringing a small notebook to dinner, writing about my day instead of just staring at my phone.
Host: Would you recommend solo travel to someone considering it?
Guest: [warmly] It can suit some adults, but prepare carefully, keep trusted contact, and change plans if a place feels unsafe.
Host: What's the one thing you'd tell your nervous self from before this trip?
Guest: I would say: learn the risks, make a safe plan, and know that coming home early is allowed.
